(1²+1²)/1!=2=1/1!+1/1!,

(3²+4²)/5!=25/120=5/24=1/3!+1/4!,

We invoke and prove the required classification.

Factorial classification lemma. For positive integers a≤b and c, (1) with (x,y,z) replaced by (a,b,c) holds exactly when (a,b,c)=(1,1,1) or (3,4,5).

Proof. Put P=(a+1)(a+2)⋯b, with P=1 if a=b. Since b!=a!P, cancellation reduces the equation to

(a²+b²)P=c!\left(1+P^{-1}\right).  (2)

(a²+b²)a!/(a!+b!)<1,

unless b=a+1. Thus b=a+1. Substitution into (2), followed by cancellation, leaves

(a²+(a+1)²)a!=(a+1)!(a!+(a+1)!),

whose consecutive-factor comparison gives a=3 and c=5. Hence the only cases are (1,1,1) and (3,4,5). ∎

Applying the lemma and restoring the interchange symmetry yields

\boxed{(x,y,z)=(1,1,1),\ (3,4,5),\ (4,3,5)}.
